instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of "lobbyist" turns on being employed/receiving economic consideration and, if duties are not exclusively lobbying, making lobbying communications on at least 5 days in a reporting period, but it sets no dollar compensation threshold.
The statute’s definition of "lobbyist" contains no expenditure-based trigger for lobbyist status or licensing.
Expense reporting under § 13.68 is imposed on registered principals and does not establish any per-item de minimis threshold for itemizing individual expenditures on a lobbyist spending report.

A principal must register only after exceeding $500 in a calendar year for non-exempt lobbying, and principals anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and then are not subject to licensing/registration/reporting if true.

The only time-based exclusion in the disclosure provisions is for certain non-lobbyist employees who devote not more than 10 hours to lobbying during a reporting period, not a percentage-of-compensated-time exemption for lobbyists.
